_metadata.source: SDMMC Controller (3MCR) — SPC58 H-Line Reference Manual

figures.title: 3MCR controller
figures.abstract: This block diagram shows the 3MCR host controller architecture for SDMMC, consisting of master/target AHB interfaces, PIO/DMA controller, block buffer FIFO, control blocks (RECV_CTRL, CMD_CTRL, XMT_CTRL, CLK_GEN), and RX/TX flops connecting to the SDMMC interface.

figures.title: Feedback clock selection
figures.abstract: This block diagram shows the SDMMC feedback clock selection mechanism with two paths: Path A for direct clock output (up to 12MHz default speed) and Path B using a 4-input multiplexer for feedback clock selection supporting high speed modes up to 50MHz.

figures.title: SDMA System address / Argument 2 register (SDMASYSADDR)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit SDMASYSADDR register layout at offset 0x0000, containing a single SDMA_SYSADDRESS field spanning all bits 0-31 with read/write access and a reset value of 0.

figures.title: Block size register (BLOCKSIZE)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit BLOCKSIZE register layout at offset 0x0004, containing two fields: SDMA_BUFBOUNDARY (bits 3:0) for host SDMA buffer size configuration and XFER_BLOCKSIZE (bits 15:4) for transfer block size specification, with all bits reset to 0.

figures.title: Block count register (BLOCKCOUNT)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit BLOCKCOUNT register layout at offset 0x0006, containing the XFER_BLOCKCOUNT field (bits 15:0) used for block count transfer operations in the SDMMC controller, with read/write access and a reset value of 0.

figures.title: Argument 1 register (ARGUMENT1)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit ARGUMENT1 register layout at offset 0x0008, containing a single COMMAND_ARGUMENT1 field spanning bits 31:0 with read/write access and a reset value of zero.

figures.title: Transfer mode register (TRANSFERMODE)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit TRANSFERMODE register layout at offset 0x000C with control fields for DMA enable, block count enable, auto command enable, data transfer direction, and multi-block select in bits 10-15, while bits 0-9 are reserved zeros.

figures.title: Command register (COMMAND)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit COMMAND register layout at offset 0x000E for the SDMMC controller, with fields for command index, command type, data present, index/CRC check enable, and response type.

figures.title: Response n register (RESPONSEn)
figures.abstract: The RESPONSEn register is a 16-bit read-only register at offset 0x0010 + n*0x2 (where n=0 to 7) containing the COMMAND_RESPONSE field that stores command response data, with all bits reset to 0.

figures.title: Data port register (DATAPORT)
figures.abstract: The DATAPORT register is a 32-bit read/write register at offset 0x0020 containing the PIOBUFRDDATA field spanning all bits [31:0], with a reset value of 0x00000000.

figures.title: Present state register (PRESENTSTATE)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit PRESENTSTATE register layout at offset 0x0024, which contains read-only status bits indicating the current state of SDMMC DAT lines, CMD line, card detection, write protection, and DMA transfer activity.

figures.title: Host control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 8-bit Host control 1 register (HOSTCONTROL1) at offset 0x0028, containing fields for data width, high-speed enable, DMA select, extended data width, CD test level, and CD signal select configuration.

figures.title: Power control register (POWERCONTROL)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 8-bit POWERCONTROL register at offset 0x0029 with read/write access, containing the PWRCTRL_SDBUSVOLTAGE field (bits 4:6) and SD_BUS_POWER field (bit 7), all reset to 0.

figures.title: Block gap control register (BLOCKGAPCONTROL)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 8-bit BLOCKGAPCONTROL register layout at offset 0x002A with read/write access, containing fields for block gap control, boot acknowledgment, boot mode, interrupt, SPI mode, and wait control functions.

figures.title: Wakeup control register (WAKEUPCONTROL)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 8-bit WAKEUPCONTROL register layout at offset 0x002B, with bits 5-7 controlling wakeup event enables for SD card removal, insertion, and interrupt respectively, while bits 0-4 are reserved as zero.

figures.title: Clock control register (CLOCKCONTROL)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit CLOCKCONTROL register layout at offset 0x002C for the SDMMC controller, containing fields for internal clock enable, clock stability status, SD/MMC clock enable, and clock frequency selection bits.

figures.title: Timeout control register (TIMEOUTCONTROL)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 8-bit TIMEOUTCONTROL register layout at offset 0x002E, with bits 7:4 containing the TIMEOUT_CTRVALUE field and bits 3:0 reserved as zeros, with read/write access and a reset value of 0x00.

figures.title: Software reset register (SOFTWARERESET)
figures.abstract: Register layout diagram showing the 8-bit SOFTWARERESET register at offset 0x002F with three writable software reset control bits (SWRESET_FOR_ALL, SWRESET_FOR_CMD, SWRESET_FOR_DAT) in bits 7-5 and reserved bits 4-0, all with reset value of 0.

figures.title: Normal interrupt status register (NORMALINTRSTS)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit NORMALINTRSTS register layout at offset 0x0030, containing interrupt status flags for SD/MMC card operations including command complete, transfer complete, card insertion/removal, buffer ready, and boot-related status bits, most of which are write-1-to-clear (w1c).

figures.title: Error interrupt status register (ERRORINTRSTS)
figures.abstract: A 16-bit error interrupt status register (ERRORINTRSTS) at offset 0x0032 showing various error status bits for SDMMC controller including timeout, CRC, end bit, and index errors for both command and data operations, with write-1-to-clear (w1c) functionality.

figures.title: Normal interrupt status enable register (NORMALINTRSTSENA)
figures.abstract: A 16-bit read/write register at offset 0x0034 that enables normal interrupt status bits for the SDMMC controller, with individual enable bits for various interrupt sources including card insertion, card removal, and card interrupt status.

figures.title: Error interrupt status enable register (ERRORINTRSTSENA)
figures.abstract: Register layout diagram for the ERRORINTRSTSENA (Error interrupt status enable register) at offset 0x0036, showing 16 bits with various ERRORINTRSTS_ENABLEREGBITx fields for enabling error interrupt status, with Read/Write access and reset value of 0.

figures.title: Normal interrupt signal enable register (NORMALINTRSIGENA)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit NORMALINTRSIGENA register layout at offset 0x0038, which controls normal interrupt signal enable bits for an SD/MMC controller, with all bits reset to 0.

figures.title: Error interrupt signal enable register (ERRORINTRSIGENA)
figures.abstract: A 16-bit read/write error interrupt signal enable register (ERRORINTRSIGENA) at offset 0x003A with enable bits for various error interrupt signals, where bit 4 and bits 0-2 are fixed at 0, and all other bits reset to 0.

figures.title: Auto CMD error status enable register (AUTOCMDERRSTS)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit AUTOCMDERRSTS register layout at offset 0x003C, which contains error status enable bits for Auto CMD operations including NEXTERROR (bit 8), INDEXERROR (bit 11), ENDBITERROR (bit 12), CRCERROR (bit 13), TIMEOUTERROR (bit 14), and NOTEXECERROR (bit 15).

figures.title: Host control 2 register (HOSTCONTROL2)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit HOSTCONTROL2 register layout at offset 0x003E for the SDMMC controller, containing fields for UHS mode selection, voltage signaling, driver strength, execute tuning, sampling clock selection, asynchronous interrupt enable, and preset value enable.

figures.title: Capabilities[31:0] register (CAPABILITIES31_0)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit CAPABILITIES31_0 register layout at offset 0x0040, which is a read-only register containing HD implementation-specific capability fields including clock frequencies, voltage support, DMA support, and maximum block length settings.

figures.title: Capabilities[63:32] register (CAPABILITIES63_32)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit CAPABILITIES63_32 register layout at offset 0x0044, containing read-only configuration fields for SPI block mode support, SPI mode support, re-tuning modes, and DDR mode support capabilities of the SDMMC controller.

figures.title: Maximum current capabilities[31:0] register (MAXCURRENTCAP31_0)
figures.abstract: A 32-bit read-only register layout showing the maximum current capabilities for 3.3V, with bits 31:24 containing CORECFG_MAXCURRENT3P3V field and bits 23:0 reserved, all reset to zero.

figures.title: Maximum current capabilities[63:32] register (MAXCURRENTCAP63_32)
figures.abstract: Register layout for MAXCURRENTCAP63_32 at offset 0x004C showing a 32-bit read-only register with all bits reserved and reset to 0.

figures.title: Preset value n register (PRESETVALUEn)
figures.abstract: A 16-bit read-only register layout for PRESETVALUEn showing bits 0-15, all initialized to 0 on reset, with offset calculated as 0x0060 + n*0x2 where n ranges from 0 to 7.

figures.title: Slot interrupt status register (SLOTINTRSTS)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit SLOTINTRSTS (Slot interrupt status) register layout at offset 0x00FC, which is read-only with bit 15 containing the SDHCHOSTIF_SLOTINTRSTS field and bits 14-0 reserved as zeros with reset value of 0.

figures.title: Host controller version register (HOSTCONTROLLERVER)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit read-only HOSTCONTROLLERVER register at offset 0x00FE, containing the SDHC vendor version number (bits 0-5) and specification version number (bits 6-15) fields with a reset value of 0x4008.

figures.title: Force event for auto CMD error status register
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit write-only FORCEEVENTFORAUTOCMDERRSTS register at offset 0x0050, which allows software to force various Auto CMD12 error status bits including NOTEXEC, TIMEOUTERR, CRCERR, ENDBITERR, INDEXERR, and CMDNOTISSUED errors.

figures.title: Force event for error interrupt status register (FORCEEVENTFORERRINTSTS)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 16-bit FORCEEVENTFORERRINTSTS register layout at offset 0x0052, which is a write-only register used to force error interrupt events for testing purposes, with bits 15-6 controlling various error types (CMD timeout, CRC, end bit, index errors and data errors) and bits 5-0 reserved.

figures.title: ADMA Error status register (ADMAERRSTS)
figures.abstract: An 8-bit read-only ADMA Error status register (ADMAERRSTS) at offset 0x0054 showing bit fields for ADMAERRORSTATE (bit 7) and ADMALENMISMATCHERR (bit 5), with all bits reset to 0.

figures.title: ADMA System address n register (ADMASYSADDRn)
figures.abstract: A 16-bit read/write register layout showing the ADMA System address register (ADMASYSADDRn) with bits 15:0 containing the ADMA_SYSADDRESS field, all bits reset to 0, located at offset 0x0058 + n*0x2 where n ranges from 0 to 3.

figures.title: Boot timeout control register (BOOTTIMEOUTCNT)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit BOOTTIMEOUTCNT register layout at offset 0x0070, containing a single field BOOT_TIMEOUTCNT spanning bits 0-31 for configuring the boot data timeout counter value, with a reset value of 0.

figures.title: Core configuration register (CORE_CONFIG)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit CORE_CONFIG register layout at offset 0x0208, containing fields for SDMMC protocol clock frequency configuration (BASECLKFREQ_SDMMC_CLK), ADMA2 selection (CORECFG_ADMA2SUPPORT, CORECFG_ASYNCHINTRSUPPORT), slot type (CORECFG_SLOTTYPE), and maximum IO current value (MAXCURRENT_3P3V).

figures.title: Feedback clock selection register (FB_CLK_SEL)
figures.abstract: A 32-bit read/write register at offset 0x0210 used to program the feedback clock source, with the FEEDBACKCLK_SEL field occupying bits 30-31 and all other bits reserved as 0.

figures.title: Debug status 1 register (DBG_STA1)
figures.abstract: A 32-bit read-only debug status register (DBG_STA1) at offset 0x0220 containing the DMADEBUGBUS field spanning all 32 bits, providing a 16-bit wide DMA Control debug bus for software debugging, with all bits reset to 0.

figures.title: Debug status 2 register (DBG_STA2)
figures.abstract: A 32-bit read-only debug status register (DBG_STA2) at offset 0x0224 containing the CMDDEBUGBUS field in bits 31:16 and reserved zero bits in bits 15:0, used for CMD Control debug bus software debugging.

figures.title: Debug status 3 register (DBG_STA3)
figures.abstract: This figure shows the 32-bit read-only Debug status 3 register (DBG_STA3) at offset 0x0228, containing the TXDDEBUGBUS field in bits 23-24 for TXD module control debug bus software debugging, with all bits reset to 0.

figures.title: Debug status 4 register (DBG_STA4)
figures.abstract: A 32-bit read-only debug status register (DBG_STA4) at offset 0x022C showing the RXDDEBUGBUS0 field in bits 24-31 for RXD module control debug bus software debugging, with all other bits reserved and reset to zero.

figures.title: Debug status 5 register (DBG_STA5)
figures.abstract: A 32-bit read-only debug status register (DBG_STA5) at offset 0x0230, with RXDDEBUGBUS1 field in bits 31:24 and reserved zero bits in the remaining positions, used for RXD module control debug bus feedback during software debugging.

figures.title: Data transfer using DAT line sequence (not using DMA)
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the SDMMC data transfer sequence using the DAT line without DMA, showing the step-by-step process for configuring registers, handling command completion, managing buffer read/write operations, and completing single/multi-block or infinite block transfers.

figures.title: Data transfer using DAT line sequence (using DMA)
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the step-by-step sequence for performing a data transfer using the DAT line with DMA on an SDMMC controller, covering register configuration, command execution, interrupt handling, and status clearing operations.

figures.title: ADMA transaction flow
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the ADMA (Advanced DMA) transaction flow for the SDMMC controller, showing the sequence of register configurations, command execution, and interrupt handling steps from descriptor table creation through transfer completion or error handling.

figures.title: Synchronous abort transaction
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the synchronous abort transaction process for an SDMMC controller, showing the sequence from setting a block gap request through clearing transfer status, issuing abort command, and performing software resets until the DAT and CMD line reset flags are cleared.

figures.title: Asynchronous abort
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the asynchronous abort procedure for the SDMMC controller, showing the sequence of issuing an abort command, setting software reset for DAT and CMD lines, and polling until both reset flags are cleared.

figures.title: Boot code access flow diagram
figures.abstract: This flowchart illustrates the boot code access sequence for the SDMMC controller, showing the initialization steps from power-on reset through host controller configuration, boot data reading, and the decision flow for completing or continuing the boot read operation.

figures.title: Multiple-block write timing
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the SDMMC multiple-block write operation sequence including command, data transmission with CRC on DAT0 and DAT1-7 lines, status responses, and busy signaling between consecutive write blocks.

figures.title: Multiple block read
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the multiple block read operation for SDMMC, illustrating the host command sequence with NCR cycles followed by response and multiple data blocks on DAT0-7 lines with NAC cycles between consecutive read data transfers.

figures.title: Boot operation timing with termination between consecutive data blocks
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the boot operation sequence for SDMMC with termination occurring between consecutive 512-byte data blocks, illustrating the CMD and DAT0-7 signal transitions including optional timing parameters t_BA, t_BD, N_AC, N_ST, and N_CD.

figures.title: Boot operation timing with termination during transfer
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the boot operation sequence with termination occurring during data transfer, illustrating the CMD and DAT0-7 signal transitions from boot request recognition through data transfer to boot request completion with CMD1.

figures.title: Alternative boot operation, termination between consecutive data blocks
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the SDMMC alternative boot operation sequence where termination occurs between consecutive 512-byte data blocks, with CMD0 (argument 0xFFFFFFFA) initiating the boot and CMD0/CMD1 sequence completing the operation.

figures.title: Alternative boot operation, termination during transfer
figures.abstract: This timing diagram shows the alternative boot operation sequence for SDMMC where termination occurs during a data transfer, with CMD0 (argument 0xFFFFFFFA) interrupting an ongoing 512-byte block transfer before completing with CMD1.
